chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent and kept witnesses upon her divorce. Then he returned and stayed with the woman for months, not informing her of her divorce. Then the woman claimed pregnancy, so the man said, 'I have divorced you, and I kept witnesses upon your divorce.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is necessitated upon him, and his word is not accepted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child's lineage if the father divorces his wife in his absence, returns, lives with her, and then denies the pregnancy?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'istidlal' (presumption of paternity) by prioritizing the physical reality of cohabitation over the man's unilateral declaration of divorce. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on protecting the lineage and rights of the child, ensuring that a husband cannot evade paternal responsibility through technicalities when he has maintained marital relations without explicit notification of the divorce.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorces his wife and he is absent, and keeps witnesses upon divorcing her. Then he comes over, so he lives with the woman for months, not letting her know of her divorce. Then the woman claims the pregnancy, so the man says, ‘I had divorced you, and I kept witnesses upon your divorce’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The child would be necessitated upon him, and his words would not be accepted’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife when he is absent from her. He arranges witnesses about his divorce; then he comes home and stays with her for months without informing her of divorce and the woman claims to have become pregnant but the man says. ‘I had divorced you in the presence of witnesses. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is responsible for the child and his words are not accepted.’”
